extracted.intended_audience: researchers and academics who act as journal peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: ethical peer review for journal manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers serving as peer reviewers about their ethical responsibilities when accepting and conducting manuscript reviews, including confidentiality, conflict disclosure, competence, and the reviewer’s role in flagging misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of unpublished manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are trusted not to share or reuse the contents of the unpublished manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose manuscript content, ideas, data, or use them for your own work; treat the submission as confidential material entrusted by the editor and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑use / no appropriation of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must not reuse or appropriate the contents or ideas of an unpublished manuscript for their own benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid incorporating authors' ideas, data, or analyses into your own research or passing them to others before publication; refrain from using privileged information gained through review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an honest assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers have obligations to provide an honest assessment of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess manuscripts fairly and objectively, report strengths and weaknesses transparently, and base judgments on evidence and expertise rather than personal preference or rivalry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and highlight potential conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should highlight potential conflicts of interest when conducting reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any relationships, financial interests, or other factors that might bias your review to the editor and, where appropriate, recuse yourself from the review if the conflict is significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept reviews only when you have time and knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should only accept a review request if they have the time – and knowledge – required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline or suggest alternatives if you lack sufficient subject-matter expertise or cannot complete the review within the requested timeframe; timely completion is part of ethical reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role in detecting plagiarism, fraud and other ethics issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can play an important role in flagging problem submissions, but the primary burden of ensuring a manuscript is free of plagiarism, fraud and other ethics issues does not rest on reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect plagiarism, data fabrication, or other misconduct, alert the editor with evidence or concerns; do not assume full responsibility for investigation—editors and institutions carry the main burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify limits of reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: There is ambiguity about whether reviewers have a duty to identify authors’ unethical behavior; reviewers should understand the limits of their role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that while you should flag suspected ethical problems, systematic policing or forensic checks are typically the responsibility of editors/publishers/institutions rather than individual reviewers.
